newsitem.title: UK: Conoco delays UK MacCulloch oilfield start to mid-year.
newsitem.headline: Conoco delays UK MacCulloch oilfield start to mid-year.

text.p: Conoco said on Wednesday it had delayed the start of its 50,000 barrel a day (bpd) U.K. North Sea MacCulloch development until the middle of the year.
First crude from the 58 million barrel field would be delayed until the end of the second quarter, Conoco UK general manager for extraction, Roger Ramshaw, said.
Conoco originally had scheduled to bring the field on stream in December of last year, but in November pushed back the project to the first quarter of 1997.
Ramshaw said the floating production and storage offtake vessel Dagmar Maersk would set sail for the field from a Teeside dockyard next month.
Conoco holds a 60 percent share in MacCulloch in partnership with LASMO plc, which holds the remaining 40 percent.

The crude, similar to North Sea benchmark Brent, will be transported to Britain's Flotta terminal in the Orkney islands but the FPSO will also be equipped to load shuttle tankers if pipeline capacity to Flotta is not available.
